title: Tutorials: the Video track
goal:
What to do with a recording: trim it to the part that matters and get it out in a form you can send.

The guides in this track: Trim a recording; Export MP4, GIF or HEIC.
notes:
One of the seven track tasks. Depends on the framework task and on the Help menu IA task.

What this track is for: Smallest track, and last in the order. Covers the Video menu (EditorCommands.swift:249 onwards) and PhotonzMedia. Trimming is destructive on save in a way the rest of the app is not - a save bakes the edits into the stored file, with the original kept alongside and Revert to Original as the way back - so the trim guide has to say that plainly rather than leave somebody to find out.

Write the guides as DATA in the catalogue. If a guide in this track cannot be expressed without new framework machinery, that is a finding: file it against the framework rather than special casing it here, and say so in the audit.

---
SHARED CONTEXT for every tutorials task (asked for by the user on 2026-09-12):

The user's words: "I would like a help > tutorials > * set of guides which walks you through basics of various features. Maybe a nice getting started tutorial, maybe a 'building components' walkthrough, etc. ... And maybe a first run experience which lets you get an intro to the app, or just gogogo. Use the design clickthroughs as inspiration, where you have pointers and can point to various parts of the application. Build a nice framework for defining these walkthroughs so that we can extend it over time. I'd like the tutorials system to be well organized and not just a long list of things."

The agreed shape (settled in the intake conversation, 2026-09-12):
- TRACKS, not a flat list. Help > Tutorials holds "Take the Tour" plus one SUBMENU per track, and a Tutorials window is the hub. The tracks are: Basics, Redlining, Looks, Colours & Styles, Building UI, Components, Video.
- A guide is DATA, not code: a Codable value in PhotonzCore describing steps. Adding a guide means adding data to the catalogue, and the menu, the window and the progress list all pick it up with no UI edited. That is the whole point of the framework and the thing that makes it extensible.
- Steps POINT AT REAL UI, clickthrough-style: a callout with a pointer aimed at a named control, not a page of prose.
- Design doc: docs/design/tutorials.md is the source of truth for the framework and the track list, written by the foundation task and extended by the rest.

THE TRAP that will waste a runner's day if it is not read first: the app already has a registry of named UI targets, the playtest harness (playtestControl / playtestField / steady names, Sources/Photonz/Playtest/PanelTarget.swift). It looks like exactly the right thing to reuse and it is NOT USABLE here: it is compiled out of the shipping build (Scripts/build-app.sh defines PHOTONZ_PLAYTEST for the dev and probe variants only, see docs/design/playtest-harness.md, "Who can run it"), and PanelTarget.swift:141 onwards is the no-op stub release actually gets. Tutorials ship to users, so the anchor registry has to be its own thing that is compiled IN for release. Model it on the playtest one - especially the STEADY NAME idea at PanelTarget.swift:126-138, a name taken off the model rather than off the copy, so rewording a label cannot break a guide - but do not depend on it.

Existing surfaces a tutorial entry point must fit with rather than duplicate:
- The Welcome window (Sources/Photonz/Welcome/WelcomeController.swift), first-run permissions setup, re-reachable from the menu-bar menu as "Welcome & Permissions...". It already owns first launch.
- The empty-editor onboarding card (Sources/Photonz/EditorView.swift:590-615): open a file, capture a rectangle, paste an image, blank canvas.
- There is NO Help menu in the app today: EditorCommands.swift declares Capture, Image, Video, Layer and the standard groups, and macOS supplies the default Help menu. Help > Tutorials has to be created.

Queue-driven app work targets the NEXT release unless the task says otherwise (CLAUDE.md), and a Current change is not finished until Next has it.
acceptance: Every guide in the track exists in the catalogue as data and appears under its track in the Help menu and the Tutorials window with no UI edited
Every guide runs start to finish in the real app, pointing at real controls, each one captured step by step in the audit
Every guide is short: a person can finish one in the time the entry claims, and the claim is measured rather than guessed
Every step points at something a person can actually see at that moment: nothing points at a control that is scrolled out of view, disabled or behind a closed panel without opening it first
A guide that needs something on the canvas brings its own sample document rather than depending on what the person has open
Copy obeys the repo rules: no em dashes, nothing about the tooling that built it, plain short human sentences
Every guide is checked with the features it teaches flagged off as well as on, and behaves sensibly either way
Audit under queue/audits/ with each guide captured step by step, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: adversarial review, before building. The video editor is a DIFFERENT window from everything the tutorials framework has taught in so far (VideoEditorView + VideoEditorState: an AVKit preview with one floating glass controller), and four things fall out of that.

1. The framework is bolted to EditorState. TutorialController takes an EditorState, prepares with it, asks it what is already true, and follows its window. None of that exists in a video window. This is the framework machinery the task warned about: it gets a host abstraction rather than a second controller, and the audit says so.

2. There is nothing to trim. Every other sample is a drawing; this one has to be a real recording written to disk before the window opens, or the guide depends on what the person happens to have recorded, which acceptance forbids.

3. The controller HIDES. It fades 2.4s after the pointer leaves it, and every control the trim guide points at lives on it. A ring round a faded out button is the worst failure this framework has, so a running guide pins the controller visible. Reveal only, same rule as every other prepare.

4. Nothing in a menu can be ringed, and Export runs a MODAL save panel (panel.runModal). So the export guide rings the Export button and names what is inside it rather than walking anybody into a dialog that blocks the card. It ends on Copy instead, which is what most people actually want when they say send this to somebody, and needs no dialog at all.

Two more, decided here: the window AUTOPLAYS when it opens, so a first step saying press space to play would come up already true every time. The first two cards describe the clip and teach the transport instead, and nothing waits until the scissors. And trimming is destructive on save, so the last card says that plainly and does NOT make anybody save.
The walk harness has no idea video windows exist (8k lines, all EditorState), so a walk per guide means teaching it to adopt one. Third piece of machinery.

built. Two guides as DATA in the catalogue (trim-a-recording, export-a-recording), and the three pieces of framework the track really needed, each added where the difference is rather than special cased in the guide.

Framework: TutorialHost, a protocol with three questions on it (what window am I in, reveal this, is this already so). The controller held an EditorState and asked it those directly; now both editors answer and the controller never asks which it is holding. Anchors for the recording's window (TutorialAnchor.video), and five triggers wired in VideoEditorState: trimModeOpened, trimStartMoved, trimEndMoved, trimApplied, recordingCopied. The two handles get an event each so dragging the left one twice cannot satisfy the step about the right one.

A running guide pins the floating controller up (isTutorialRunning, counted by `editing`, respected by forceHide). Without it every control the trim guide points at fades out 2.4s after the pointer leaves. Reveal only, and the fade comes straight back when the guide closes.

TutorialSampleRecording writes a real 8 second MP4 to the caches folder before the window opens, fresh on every start because the guide teaches that saving bakes the trim in. Two seconds of dead air at each end so trimming it has a point. It draws its filling bar along the very top edge and its counter in the left column, both clear of where a card sits: the first cut put the moving part in the centre, which is exactly where the card telling you to watch it goes.

Harness: adoptRecording takes over a window with no editor in it, waitFor tutorialStep no longer insists on an editor, and the callout's own buttons work with none. A recording's window is left VISIBLE for the walk, unlike every other: the offscreen render draws the video black and the glass controller as nearly nothing, and a capture of a zero alpha window comes back blank.

Verified: 6155 tests green. tutorial-trim-a-recording-walk and tutorial-export-a-recording-walk drive every step of both guides in the real app with real screen captures, no anchor unresolved in either. tutorial-trim-a-recording-skipped-walk skips every waiting step to prove the last card stands on its own with no trim made and so no save button to ring. All 30 tutorial walks pass, including the hub walk, which reads the Tutorials window aloud and finds both new guides: acceptance item one, with no UI edited. Sweep requested because the host change and the harness change are under every walk.

Two guides shipped as data (Trim a recording, Export MP4 GIF or HEIC) plus the framework they needed: TutorialHost so a guide can run over a recording's window, video anchors and five triggers, and a real sample MP4 written before the window opens. Verified: 6155 tests green, both guides walked end to end in the real app with real screen captures and no unresolved anchor, a third walk proves the skipped path strands nobody, all 30 tutorial walks pass including the hub walk that reads both new guides out with no UI edited.
